generator.program.note: The program the authors chose to grow this taxon's shrub species (named in each species' spec until G2.3a moved it here).

traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 1926), family 54 Buxaceae, under which he kept Simmondsia, APG's only genus of Simmondsiaceae: evergreen shrubs; leaves leathery, simple, without stipules (Simmondsia's opposite and entire, by his key); sepals and no petals; ovary superior, 3-celled; Simmondsia's fruit a capsule opening by three valves. Abrams's flora (vol. 3, 1951) agrees on the opposite, entire, evergreen leaves, the sepals (usually 5) and the capsule.

traits.sexual_system.note: Wikipedia's article Jojoba (read 2026-10-13): the plants are male or female, hermaphrodites very rare. Abrams (vol. 3, 1951) calls the genus monoecious, which later floras do not follow.
